label: Chips
words: It sells AI chips, and two of the chairmen have bills on their export. Mast's, his committee says, "applies long-standing congressional oversight to exports of America's sensitive, military-enhancing AI chips"; it has passed his committee and no further, and Moolenaar's has not left committee. Mast, in the release of Jan 21, 2026: "Companies like Nvidia are requesting to sell millions of advanced AI chips, which are the cutting edge of warfare, to Chinese military companies like Alibaba and Tencent."
q: Companies like Nvidia are requesting to sell millions of advanced AI chips || applies long-standing congressional oversight to exports of America's sensitive, military-enhancing AI chips || Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 42 - 2. || Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

label: Now also AI models
words: It also releases open AI models, with data and tools. Its release of Dec 15, 2025: "NVIDIA is the first to release a collection of state-of-the-art open models, training datasets and reinforcement learning environments and libraries"; the same release describes developers using open models alongside "proprietary models for state-of-the-art reasoning". A trade report of Oct 16, 2026 says its newest models show it "reinforcing its own GPU infrastructure while supporting the open source community."
q: NVIDIA is the first to release a collection of state-of-the-art open models, training datasets and reinforcement learning environments and libraries || December 15, 2025 || proprietary models for state-of-the-art reasoning || reinforcing its own GPU infrastructure while supporting the open source community || 2026-10-16

label: On the Senate's bill
words: TechSpot, Sep 4, 2025: "Nvidia has since posted a statement opposing the GAIN AI Act. The company says it is comparable to the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule that was rescinded in May, and part of an attempt to overturn Trump's AI Action Plan". It also reported Nvidia's statement "that H20 sales have not reduced its supply of H100, H200, or Blackwell GPUs". Of that rule Huang had said, as Fortune quoted him on May 2, 2025: "the U.S. semiconductor industry is being pushed out of China, the world's largest market."
q: Nvidia has since posted a statement opposing the GAIN AI Act. label: AI models
words: It makes the Claude AI models and runs them on other companies' chips: "Currently, Anthropic uses a large number of chips, including Nvidia and AMD GPUs, Google TPUs, and Amazon Trainium hardware" (Data Center Dynamics, Aug 6, 2026).
q: Currently, Anthropic uses a large number of chips, including Nvidia and AMD GPUs, Google TPUs, and Amazon Trainium hardware || August 06, 2026

label: Now also a chip-design team
words: In Aug 2026 its spokesperson confirmed "that the company was building an in-house silicon team to design custom chips for Claude", calling it "the latest step in our multi-chip approach" and saying the company would continue deploying a "diversified hardware stack". The report is of a design team: it does not describe finished chips, or chips for sale.
q: confirmed that the company was building an in-house silicon team to design custom chips for Claude || the latest step in our multi-chip approach || and that the company would continue deploying a "diversified hardware stack."

label: On export controls
words: It asks for tighter limits on chip exports. Its co-founder to Moolenaar's committee on Jun 25, 2025, before either House bill was introduced: the government should be "maintaining and strengthening export controls of advanced semiconductors to China". That is its general position, not a statement on either bill.
q: maintaining and strengthening export controls of advanced semiconductors to China || 2025-10-31 || 2025-12-18

label: May 1, 2025
words: After Anthropic argued for tighter controls and described chip smuggling, an Nvidia spokesperson said American firms should "rise to the challenge, rather than tell tall tales that large, heavy, and sensitive electronics are somehow smuggled in 'baby bumps' or 'alongside live lobsters,'" and: "America cannot manipulate regulators to capture victory in AI."
q: rise to the challenge, rather than tell tall tales that large, heavy, and sensitive electronics are somehow smuggled in 'baby bumps' or 'alongside live lobsters,' || America cannot manipulate regulators to capture victory in AI || 2025-05-01

label: Also partners
words: Reported on Nov 10, 2026: Anthropic said seven companies, Nvidia among them, had agreed to buy $26 billion of its stock between them, in a private sale at the price of its public offering. Nvidia's own share is not given. Anthropic also runs Claude partly on Nvidia chips.
q: Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to purchase $26 billion || in a private placement at a price per share equal to the IPO price || including Nvidia and AMD GPUs

label: Its own account
words: Announcing its first gift to Public First Action on Feb 12, 2026, it said of the policies it backs: "Nor are they for the benefit of Anthropic as an AI developer—effective AI governance means more scrutiny of companies like ours, not less." That is the company's statement; no record here tests it.
